questions.prompt: In the context of Oracle Fusion Financials, what does the acronym SLA refer to, and what does it actually do?
options: Subledger Accounting — the engine that converts subledger transactions like an AP invoice or AR receipt into balanced GL journal entries using account rules
Service level agreement — a contractual turnaround-time commitment between the consulting firm and the client
Subledger Accounting — a module that bulk-loads invoices into Accounts Payable using FBDI
Standard Ledger Assignment — the process that assigns a business unit to its primary ledger
Subledger Accounting — the reporting tool used to build pixel-perfect, scheduled financial statements
Service level agreement — the internal target for how long a Create Accounting batch is allowed to run
questions.explain: SLA refers to Subledger Accounting in Oracle Fusion Financials — the engine that turns subledger transactions into balanced GL journal entries using account rules before they post, per Lesson 1's terminology glossary. Watch the overload with the everyday 'service level agreement' meaning — say which one you mean if context isn't obvious.
questions.distractorExplain: Option B is the everyday meaning of 'SLA' (service level agreement) that Lesson 1 explicitly warns is a different, commonly confused meaning. In the Oracle Financials context covered throughout this path, SLA means Subledger Accounting, not a contractual turnaround commitment.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: per Lesson 1, the COA segment that must net to zero for each legal entity — which is exactly what makes intercompany elimination possible — is called the ________ segment.
questions.explain: The balancing segment (Company, in the capstone's design) is the chart-of-accounts segment that must net to zero for each legal entity, which is what makes intercompany elimination possible.

questions.prompt: Match each implementation-phase term to what it actually is, per Lesson 6.
right: Confirms the system and its integrations work correctly, usually run by the project team
The intensive support period immediately following go-live
A working session where business users react to the actual configured system before go-live
Confirms the client's own people can do their real jobs in the new system
questions.explain: A CRP is a working session where business users react to the actual configured system before go-live. SIT confirms the system and its integrations work correctly, run by the project team. UAT confirms the client's own people can do their real jobs in the new system. Hypercare is the intensive support period immediately following go-live.

questions.prompt: Finance wants to close in three business days, but AP currently takes five days just to approve invoices. Per Lesson 4's scenario framework, what's the strongest response?
options: Point out that a three-day close target is really a statement about the approval-cycle speed, and recommend either shortening the real approval cycle or building a formal accrual process for invoices still in flight at close — without just promising three days and leaving the underlying process unchanged
Promise finance the three-day close immediately, since committing to a deadline is what builds client confidence
Tell finance the request is unreasonable and refuse to discuss a faster close until AP's approval process changes
Recommend extending the close target to five days to match AP's current approval speed, since that's the real constraint
questions.explain: Lesson 4 treats this as separating the symptom (the three-day target) from the real constraint (a five-day approval cycle), recommending either shortening the real approval cycle or building a standard accrual process for invoices still in flight — not just promising a deadline without changing the process that makes it unrealistic.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about Payables matching and invoice holds, per Lesson 3.
options: 3-way matching adds the receipt to the comparison, confirming goods or services were actually received before payment
2-way matching is typically used for services or situations where a receipt step doesn't apply
Releasing a hold without resolving the underlying discrepancy just defers the same problem to the next close
Oracle only evaluates a manually applied hold — matching, tax, quantity, and price holds don't exist
3-way matching is primarily used for services, since services carry the highest payment risk
questions.explain: 3-way matching adds the receipt step and is used for physical goods (raw materials, MRO parts) where paying before receipt is a real risk; 2-way fits services or cases without a receipt step. Oracle evaluates several hold types — matching, tax, quantity, price, or manual — not only manual holds. Releasing a hold without fixing the real discrepancy just defers the same problem to the next close.

questions.prompt: Put these steps of the troubleshooting discipline named in Lesson 5 in the correct order.
items: Isolate the problem to something specific and provable
Confirm it with real evidence — logs, reports, diagnostics, not a hunch
Fix it narrowly rather than overcorrecting
questions.explain: Lesson 5 names this four-step discipline explicitly: isolate, confirm, fix, document — every troubleshooting lesson in this path and every fix in the capstone follows this same order.

questions.prompt: Per Lesson 7, what's the practical difference between loading data into Oracle Fusion via FBDI versus a REST API call?
options: FBDI is a batch process through interface tables suited to bulk migration or periodic uploads, while a REST API call is typically real-time and suited to integrating with another live system
FBDI and REST APIs are functionally identical — the only difference is which team configures them
REST APIs can only read data out of Oracle Fusion, never write data in
FBDI is used exclusively for Receivables, while REST APIs are used exclusively for Payables
questions.explain: FBDI is batch — prepare a file, load it through interface tables, which suits bulk data migration or periodic uploads. A REST API call is typically real-time and transactional, suited to integrating with another live system, such as an e-commerce platform pushing orders into AR.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: per Lesson 5, when an FBDI load fails partway through, the first thing to check is the load's ________, because Oracle's FBDI process reports specific row-level and column-level failures there, not just 'it failed.'
questions.explain: Lesson 5 is explicit: check the load's error log first, since FBDI reports specific row- and column-level failures there — only after isolating which rows failed and why do you decide whether to fix the source file and reload everything or just reload the failed rows.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about Oracle Fusion implementation phases, per Lesson 6.
options: SIT can pass while UAT still fails, because SIT doesn't catch a workflow that's technically correct but practically unusable for the people who run it daily
A conference room pilot (CRP) happens after go-live, during hypercare
A requirement that arrives after configuration is locked should be assessed for impact and raised through change control, not quietly squeezed in
During hypercare, a consultant's job shifts from building to rapid triage of whether an issue is a configuration gap, a training gap, or a genuine defect
Different firms and methodologies all use identical phase names, so a vendor-branded phase name is universal
questions.explain: SIT confirms technical/process correctness while UAT confirms real users can do their actual jobs, so SIT passing doesn't guarantee UAT will. A CRP happens before go-live, during configure-and-prototype, not during hypercare. A late requirement needs impact assessment and change control rather than being quietly absorbed. Hypercare shifts a consultant's role to rapid triage of configuration gap versus training gap versus defect. Phase names vary by firm and methodology — no single vendor's branded name is universal.

questions.prompt: Per Lesson 8, what three things does a strong resume bullet for this path's hands-on work name explicitly?
options: What you did, in which part of the system, with what result — action, system, outcome
The course title, the chapter number, and the lesson number
Your job title, your years of experience, and your certification status
The software vendor's name, the product version, and the release date
A list of every menu you clicked, in the order you clicked them
The client's name, the contract value, and the project timeline
questions.explain: Lesson 8's formula is action, system, outcome: what you did, in which part of the system, with what result — not a vague restatement of a course title, which is exactly what makes 'Configured a two-entity Oracle Fusion General Ledger enterprise structure...' stronger than 'Learned Oracle Fusion General Ledger.'
questions.distractorExplain: Option F names details from a real paid client engagement — a contract value and project timeline. Lesson 8 is explicit that this path's work is training and practice, not a paid client engagement, so a resume bullet should never imply client-engagement specifics that don't actually exist.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: per Lesson 9, STAR stands for Situation, Task, ________, Result.
questions.explain: STAR structures a work story as Situation, Task, Action, Result — Lesson 9 applies it to the capstone's six root causes, and Lesson 11 applies the same structure to behavioral questions generally.

questions.prompt: Match each capstone root cause from Lesson 9 to the fix that was actually applied.
left: AP — unreversed GRNI accrual on a Meridian Bearing Supply Co. PO
AR — a cash receipt misapplied to the wrong Harborview invoice
Fixed Assets — a new lathe set up under the wrong category
Cash Management — a $9,200 ACH transmission sent twice
right: Confirmed with the bank in writing, recorded their reversal, and completed the reconciliation — no GL correction needed
Processed a reclassification to the correct category and cost center, then corrected the depreciation calculation
Entered a manual reversing journal and verified the account balance zeroed out
Unapplied the receipt and reapplied it to the correct invoice
questions.explain: The GRNI accrual was fixed with a manual reversing journal. The misapplied Harborview receipt was unapplied and reapplied to the correct invoice. The mis-categorized lathe was reclassified to the correct category and cost center with depreciation corrected. The bank-side duplicate ACH was resolved entirely through bank confirmation and documentation — the one fix of the six that didn't touch the GL at all.

questions.prompt: Put these stages of Lesson 14's first-90-days framework in the correct order.
items: Days 1-30: shadow the close process and learn the client's specific environment before trying to fix anything
Days 31-60: start contributing on small, well-bounded work that someone more senior reviews before it goes live
Days 61-90: own a small workstream end to end, building trust mainly through communication
Beyond day 90: keep building hands-on reps as new, more specific problems keep surfacing
questions.explain: Lesson 14's 30/60/90-day framework moves from learning the specific environment (days 1-30), to contributing on reviewed, well-bounded work (days 31-60), to owning a defined workstream with real accountability (days 61-90) — and the learning curve doesn't stop at day 90, it just shifts to new problems.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about building a portfolio of practice work, per Lesson 10.
options: A requirements and configuration workbook is text and your own original diagrams, so it's entirely yours to share
Original SQL you wrote for reconciliation checks is genuinely yours to share in a public code repository
Screenshots of a licensed Oracle Fusion environment are always safe to publish publicly, since you personally configured the screen
An issue log written in symptom/root cause/fix/verification format demonstrates diagnosis-and-fix skill in writing, before an interview even starts
A one-page case study write-up should quote the actual Oracle Fusion screen text verbatim to prove authenticity
questions.explain: A requirements workbook and original SQL are both your own writing, so they're safe to share. Screenshots of licensed Oracle Fusion software may be covered by terms of use you don't control — Lesson 10 says to leave screenshots out of anything public when in doubt, not to treat personal configuration as automatic permission. An issue log in symptom/root cause/fix/verification format demonstrates real diagnostic skill in writing. The case study write-up is a narrative in your own words, not a transcript of screen text.

questions.prompt: Per Lesson 11, what makes a strong answer to 'tell me about a time you made a mistake'?
options: Admitting the mistake plainly in one sentence, then spending most of the answer on what you changed afterward
Spending most of the answer explaining the circumstances that made the mistake not really your fault
Choosing a vague, low-stakes example so the interviewer can't press for specifics
Apologizing extensively without describing any specific change you made afterward
questions.explain: Lesson 11 is specific: pick something real and specific, own it without over-explaining or deflecting, and emphasize what you changed afterward — not just that you apologized. A believable answer admits the mistake plainly in one sentence before moving to what you did about it.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Oracle's Cloud Applications certification tiers, per Lesson 12, is accurate?
options: Oracle has renamed tier names before — what was once a 'Foundations Associate' credential has, for several product lines, been renamed 'Process Essentials Certified,' without invalidating certifications already earned under the old name
Completing this LTV Academy path automatically issues an Oracle certification
Exam codes never change once Oracle publishes them, since Oracle Cloud Applications use fixed release versions like older on-premise software
The only authoritative source for current exam names and prerequisites is a third-party study-guide site, not Oracle itself
questions.explain: Lesson 12 is explicit that LTV Academy does not issue Oracle certifications — a real certification requires passing Oracle's own proctored exam through Oracle University. It also notes Oracle has renamed its foundational tier before (Foundations Associate to Process Essentials Certified for several product lines) without invalidating certifications already earned, and that exam codes are versioned to the year because Oracle Cloud Applications update continuously, unlike fixed-version on-premise software — so the current, authoritative source is Oracle University and Oracle CertView, not a third-party blog or study guide.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: per Lesson 13's three-question readiness check, a practice exam score should be used as a ________ check, not as the study plan itself.
questions.explain: The third readiness-check question asks whether you're using practice exams as a readiness check rather than as the study plan itself — a practice exam score tells you where the remaining gaps are, it doesn't fill them, and a passed practice exam isn't the same as being ready for the real one.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about the mistakes new consultants make in their first 90 days, per Lesson 14.
options: In days 1-30, the common mistake is assuming your training generalizes perfectly and jumping in to 'fix' something before understanding why it's set up that way
In days 31-60, the mistake to avoid is taking on ambiguous work without checking the actual requirement first
In days 61-90, the mistake to avoid is going quiet about a problem instead of raising it early
By day 90, trust is built mainly through technical correctness, with communication playing almost no role
A real client's instance is typically a blank version of what you practiced on in the capstone
questions.explain: Days 1-30's mistake is assuming training generalizes and jumping to 'fix' things prematurely; days 31-60's mistake is taking on ambiguous work without a clarifying question first; days 61-90's mistake is going quiet instead of raising a problem early. Lesson 14 says trust at day 90 comes less from technical correctness and more from communication — the opposite of the fourth option. And a real client's instance is never a blank version of the capstone environment — it has its own configuration history, quirks, and undocumented workarounds.

questions.prompt: Per Lesson 15, what's the honest trade-off between working for a staffing/consulting firm versus working in-house?
options: A consulting firm builds breadth faster across multiple clients and industries but comes with travel and billable-hour pressure; in-house builds deep institutional knowledge of one organization with more schedule stability but less variety
In-house roles always pay more than consulting firm roles
A consulting firm role guarantees faster promotion to Senior Consultant than an in-house role
There is no real difference between the two environments for a Functional Consultant
questions.explain: Lesson 15 describes a genuine trade-off, not a universally better option: a staffing/consulting firm builds breadth faster across clients and industries but comes with travel and billable-hour pressure, while in-house work builds deep institutional knowledge of one organization's configuration with more schedule stability but less variety and slower exposure to new patterns.

questions.prompt: Match each consulting career title from Lesson 15 to what it actually involves.
right: Works under supervision on well-defined configuration and support tasks
Leads a module or workstream across a full engagement and mentors more junior consultants
Owns client relationships at the engagement level and shapes overall solution design
Owns defined workstreams independently and handles client communication directly
questions.explain: A Functional Analyst works under supervision on well-defined tasks. A Functional Consultant owns defined workstreams independently and handles client communication directly. A Senior Consultant leads a module or workstream and mentors junior consultants. Lead/Principal/Practice roles own client relationships at the engagement level and shape overall solution design.
